g7_warnings.warning: Contents, References, AI-use disclosures, running headers, watermarks, QR material, and third-party figure text are not positive author-language evidence.
The Doubao disclosure covers concepts, literature, modeling suggestions, and model-building help; the disclosure itself is excluded from human-style evidence.
The Kimi disclosure covers analysis, visualization, hypothesis testing, time-series, and factor-analysis suggestions; the disclosure itself is excluded from human-style evidence.
Assumption 1's explanation repeats stable tourist-consumption behavior, which belongs to Assumption 2 rather than the stated tourist-cap premise.
The paper treats approximately tourist-correlated revenue as profit, bypassing a complete accounting model and causal evidence.
Equation (12) includes promotion y7 as a hidden cost while other government spending is handled inconsistently, creating omission or double-counting risk.
The resident-satisfaction prose names tourists exceeding a limit, but Equation (20) uses x/max(x) and contains no y1 or exceedance term.
The printed tourist-satisfaction function lists x,y1,y3,y4,y5,y6,y7, while Equation (21) only uses x,y4,y5,y6.
Equation (31) uses lambda43-lambda45 for glacier constants; Equations (54)-(56) reuse the same symbols for Hawaii pollution and New Orleans culture.
Equation (39)'s shorthand A-W is ambiguous about which intermediate variables are nonnegative.
Equation (41) reuses H for least-squares loss after Equation (7) defines H as management cost.
Gradient descent is named without a data table, fit diagnostics, initialization, learning rate, stopping rule, code, seed, or software version.
Table 2 supplies selected lambda values without sources, units, uncertainty, or the objective weights and epsilon terms required for replay.
Equation (45) drops the max-normalization denominators printed in Equation (15), changing the social objective passed to NSGA-II.
Population size, variable ranges, tournament size, crossover and mutation probabilities, distribution indexes, generation limit, seed, runtime, and code are not fully frozen.
Equations (48)-(50) are not accompanied by variable bounds, repair behavior, or an implementation trace.
Equation (52) is typographically and OCR ambiguous at the second bound term; no code is supplied to disambiguate it.
Equation (53) prints only one perturbation expression and does not clearly state the complete piecewise polynomial-mutation rule.
Figure 8 shows a Pareto surface but no selected point, candidate table, stakeholder weights, or decision rule supports the claimed comprehensive optimum.
The selected allocation reports 30 percent environmental, 40 percent infrastructure, and 20 percent promotion, leaving ten percent unexplained.
The results prose also assigns 30 percent to community development, conflicting with the 30/40/20 configuration.
The memo says an 80-dollar per-person tourism tax, while the main result reports an 8 percent tourism tax and a separate 15-dollar fee.
The memo states 30/40/30 environmental, infrastructure, and community allocations, conflicting with the summary and result allocation.
Sensitivity figures omit frozen baselines, numerical ranges, step sizes, data tables, stability criteria, and policy-rank changes.
Figure 10 provides a small response matrix without quantitative interaction metrics or uncertainty.
Claims that the model fits historical data well and accurately predicts trends lack diagnostics, a holdout set, residuals, or external outcomes.
The sensitivity section is treated as proof of effectiveness and stability although it reports only qualitative model responses.
Further Discussion proposes introducing tourist satisfaction even though S_tourist is already defined in Equation (21).
The Hawaii extension removes the glacier constraint and adds pollution without a frozen destination dataset, coefficient recalibration, or result table.
Yosemite, New Orleans, and New York adjustments are narrative parameter changes, not recalculated or externally validated results.
The 1.6 million passengers, 375 million dollars, glacier retreat, infrastructure pressure, and resident concerns require a frozen source ledger.
Stable capacity, stable consumption, proportional returns, stable resident psychology, and negligible climate variation are asserted without tests.
Exponential alcohol-restriction effects and multiple linear tourist-count relations are introduced without competing-form comparison.
Figure 5 and Equations (8)-(14) lack a reconciled accounting table linking each component to observed monetary data.
The maxima used in Equations (15), (20), and (21) are not frozen, so scales and transfer behavior cannot be reproduced.
Alpha, beta, and omega weights lack stakeholder elicitation, estimation, normalization checks, and uncertainty.
The glacier and pollution equations infer tourist-driven effects from component proxies without causal identification or lag structure.
Equations (26)-(28) mix annual and daily units and policy spending without published units or calibration diagnostics.
Equations (29)-(31) do not publish glacier-scale units, time horizon, baseline, or scientific threshold provenance.
Lambda36-lambda42 limits and minimum investments are not sourced or connected to enforceable policy budgets.
The solver presentation does not fully state whether each Z objective is maximized or minimized after normalization and sign conventions.
The selected 12,000 tourists per day is not reconciled to cruise schedules, annual x, seasonal peaks, or physical carrying-capacity data.
The selected tax, fee, and investment shares lack legal, administrative, distributional, and implementation constraints.
The stated weaknesses omit symbol collisions, accounting conflicts, normalization drift, solver reproducibility, internal inconsistencies, and AI provenance.
The memo gives recommendations without uncertainty ranges, owners, triggers, monitoring thresholds, lags, or rollback rules.
The reference list does not fully bind all contextual values, coefficients, datasets, functional forms, and transfer claims used by the paper.
